dedupe_keys.name: electrification of space heating in the texas residential sector simulated hourly consumption and peak demand scenarios ercot area

description: This Mendeley Data set, published in 2021 by Philip White, describes how energy use of a large residential sector would change if all space heating were electrified. Using actual 2016 weather for 17 Texas locations, thousands of EnergyPlus building models representing the residential stock served by the Texas grid were simulated for a base case and three electrification scenarios in which fossil-fuelled heating was replaced by reversible heat pumps of standard, high and ultra-high efficiency. Hourly consumption of each model was scaled by a factor of 230 and summed to the residential sector of the grid, with one CSV file per scenario, and daily peak demand files give the maximum hourly demand for each day. The results show the residential system peak shifting from summer to winter and lower summer consumption from efficiency gains. The data are available for free download under CC BY 4.0. Coverage is the Texas grid residential sector. Caveats: results are simulated for one weather year and rest on a single scaling factor, and full electrification is a stylised scenario. Simulation uses are winter peak demand under electrified heating for resource adequacy and cold-weather grid stress studies. Related records: data-mopo-heat-sector-timeseries gives heat pump and heat demand series for Europe.
